claims.statement: Logical epochs, event-time milliseconds, processing-time milliseconds, source offsets, and checkpoint round IDs are distinct progress domains; Epoch is a u64 logical number rather than a timestamp.

Source epoch allocation follows the recovered source registry and rejects exhaustion, while ShardDb provides a separate checked atomic allocator for direct-write epochs; allocation is not itself persistence.
SourceRuntimeCoordinator recovers the highest committed checkpoint, ignoring prepared records, before permitting owner activation; replacing an owner fences prior owner leases.

SourceRuntimeCoordinator commits input, committed checkpoint, and progress state in an M3 batch before upstream commit_offset; acknowledgement failure leaves durable local progress and blocks with a recovery diagnostic, and the named in-flight epoch limit is 64.

ShardDb::commit_epoch writes and flushes the supplied epoch unchanged before returning a scalar frontier report, with non-decreasing ordering required of callers; it does not convert a committed epoch into an exclusive next epoch.

ADR 0005 and MembershipFrontierReport define frontier F as durability of epochs strictly less than F; ClusterFrontier::has_committed_through(x) tests F >= x but documents completeness strictly before x rather than inclusive completeness of x.

The worker execution path durably commits frame.epoch through PhysicalCommitGroup, which writes the largest committed epoch itself to the shard frontier key, and then sends ExecutionProgress for that same epoch.

The service forwards aggregated frontier values unchanged in ClusterFrontierAdvanced, and workers pass the value unchanged to exchange GC, which deletes epochs inclusively through that value; this boundary differs from ADR 0005's exclusive completeness contract and requires explicit reconciliation before using membership frontiers for reclamation.

Configured frontier aggregation takes the minimum over authoritative active membership, initializes member progress as unknown, requires a value for every active member to compute a meet, and treats an empty active membership as no completeness.

Membership report admission validates version, scope, generation, active shard, and incarnation and advances member progress monotonically; the service, not the aggregator admission method, checks the reporting connection's current shard lease and envelope lease token.

Activating or replacing a member requires a supplied bootstrap epoch at least as high as current publication; activation, retirement, and guarded replacement advance generation with overflow rejection, and retirement of the last member clears publication.
Bootstrap durability and membership configuration authority remain external responsibilities: the membership API checks bootstrap epoch bounds rather than proving underlying snapshot durability.

The scalar compatibility aggregator learns membership from reports and only advances publication, which cannot safely establish completeness after admitting a lower-progress member; configured aggregators reject legacy scalar reports.

Durable frontier publisher election is optional wiring separate from local aggregation; the lease store serializes token checks, persists a strictly larger token and holder, and flushes before granting a lease, while stale acquisition is a normal race loss.
Durable membership publications are scoped by scope and generation so publisher recovery does not import a different configuration's publication.

try_publish requires publisher status and a meet, demotes on preflight token mismatch, and then uses a store assertion for current publisher fencing; the store rejects retreating writes and flushes publication before synchronized handoff reads, with RS-8002 and RS-8003 hard invariant assertions.
The scalar control-service frontier handler ingests locally, gates replies on Raft leadership, and reads cluster_frontier rather than invoking the optional durable try_publish path.

CheckpointCoordinator allocates checkpoint rounds from one with overflow rejection, reserves one separate alignment credit per registered shard, and delegates barrier injection to the caller; the barrier contract requires draining in-flight input and local operator completion before snapshotting.
ShardDb::create_checkpoint uses SlateDB Durable checkpoint scope and returns both a manifest ID and snapshot UUID, enabling exact snapshot references rather than dependence on mutable latest state.

CheckpointCoordinator validates confirmation round and shard, invokes the manifest commit callback after all pending shards confirm, and records completion only after callback success; it clears the round before calling the callback, so failure does not leave an in-place retryable pending round.

Changelog checkpoint collection requires matching round IDs, stages per-shard contributions before confirmation, snapshots contributions with the final confirmation, and asserts one contribution for every manifest shard.

CheckpointManifestStore persists shard changelog contributions separately and writes manifests using create-only object-store semantics, accepting identical repeats but rejecting conflicting content; exact loading preserves storage/corruption errors while the convenience load suppresses them.

The live worker CreateShardCheckpoint handler requires matching worker identity and active shard lease and rejects active workloads, so that entrypoint is an idle-shard backup mechanism rather than evidence of flowing-workload barrier alignment.

Checkpoint alignment defaults to 64 credits and 60 seconds, rolls back partial acquisition, and returns AlignmentTimeout on a second begin even before expiry; expired-round cleanup occurs when begin_checkpoint checks it, not through a background watchdog in this coordinator.

Checkpoint retention keeps IDs at or above latest minus horizon, so the default horizon of three retains the latest plus up to three older contiguous rounds; in-memory pruning and explicit object-store manifest/contribution GC are separate operations with strict-below-cutoff deletion.

The scalar frontier registry is capped at 100,000 shards with RS-8001 on overflow, and checkpoint alignment exposes credit fill and per-shard alignment diagnostics with dedicated exhaustion/timeout/ID-overflow errors.

FreshnessToken meet intersects source keys and join unions them; SourceProgress compares source epochs before combining equal-epoch optional watermarks, and watermark_ms takes the minimum only over present values.
FreshnessToken XORs its diagnostic hash in both meet and join, making the full token non-idempotent and unsuitable as an idempotent lattice field or membership/checkpoint authority.

The M1 and M2 formal models use bounded shard/epoch state and atomic actions with fairness annotations; their crash, replay, physical-group, publication, and membership reasoning is model-level evidence rather than live network or object-store integration coverage.

Frontier tests cover membership bootstrap guards, stale generation/incarnation, empty membership, legacy rejection and generation-scoped persistence; lease durability tests cover reopened LocalFileSystem and Docker-gated MinIO storage, while service tests exercise V2 lease admission and coordinator tests exercise collection and bounds.
